diet.text: Golden moles, rodents and other small mammals

overview.text: The Mole Snake is a big, non-venomous snake of southern and eastern Africa. It eats moles and rats, so it helps control pests.

identification.text: A firm, tube-shaped body, a small head and a pointed snout. Adults are mostly one colour, from yellow to brown or black.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Most of southern Africa, from Angola and Kenya to South Africa.

habitat.text: Lives in the old burrows of other animals.

diet.text: Golden moles, rodents and other small mammals; sometimes seabird eggs and chicks.

reproduction.text: Mates in late spring (October) and gives birth to live young.

recognise.text: Thick, plain-coloured body with a small pointed head.
